score_change_reason: I raised the score slightly because v2 presents credible de-duplication progress versus H_1674 (255-month mean|corr| 0.194, median 0.168), which weakens the strict equivalence objection from R1. I still do not approve because crisis-regime orthogonality, PIT timestamp governance, and implementation fragility remain unresolved.

agreements.point: I agree that expanding OLS beta can adapt too slowly under regime breaks, making residualization most fragile exactly at crisis transitions; the regime-conditional TDC requirement is necessary, not optional.
I agree that 2020-2026 orthogonality deterioration (mean|corr| ~0.244) and 21d turnover hard-fail risk materially threaten real diversification and live deployability.

rebuttals.point: I disagree with the implication that the diversifier axis is already established; with crisis-tail dependence still elevated (p95 |corr| ~0.447) and recent-period gate slippage, diversification is provisional, not validated.

I disagree that PIT risk is effectively closed by shift(1L)+burn-in alone; PIT compliance also requires source-level disclosure/publication timestamps and lag policy proofs, which are still missing for all inputs.
I disagree with near-certain ICIR gate confidence inferred from static decomposition; transaction costs, turnover, and regime non-stationarity can invalidate that extrapolation.

strongest_opposing_argument: The strongest challenge to my position is the empirical claim that v2 is no longer algebraically/practically duplicate of H_1674 (mean|corr| 0.194 over 255 months with high foreign-channel preservation), which directly weakens my prior linear-dominance/equivalence concern.
kill_scenarios_update: Added: (1) expanding-beta quasi-constantization under structural break can induce procyclical crisis mispositioning; (2) 21d lookback likely drives >600% turnover hard fail, erasing paper alpha after implementation costs.
